`###` headings, bullet and numbered lists, `- [ ]` and `- [x]` checkboxes, **bold**, *italic*,
`code`, and links. No tables, no blockquotes, no fenced code blocks and no images — each of them
is more code to own for something an agenda or a diary page rarely carries, and the app that first
genuinely needs one can add it then.

A checkbox is **rendered, not operated**: `- [x]` draws a ticked box, and ticking it is an edit of
the text like any other. A body is read far more often than its checklist is advanced, and a
tappable box would have to write a file from a screen whose whole point is that it writes nothing.

**It builds nodes, never HTML.** The renderer makes DOM elements and sets text, so nothing in a
body can turn into markup: a body carrying a `<script>` tag shows that tag as text. This is the
threat the CSP exists for — injected script on our own origin — and a data file in your own repo
is the likeliest thing to carry a stray angle bracket. A link is rendered only for `http`, `https`
and `mailto`; anything else stays text, so a `javascript:` URL is never something to press. Links
open in a new tab, because leaving the app would lose the view you were in.

It is hand-written rather than vendored. It is small enough to be, and the dependency table in
[TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md](TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md) asks of everything in it what would be
wrong with hand-rolling it — for this, nothing.

## Using it

- Changes appear instantly and are queued for GitHub in the background.
- A sync indicator shows: in sync / pending / error.
- Offline, the queue is kept and sent when you are back online or reopen the app.
- Editing the same entry on two devices never loses either version: the other device's version
  keeps the file, yours is kept beside it and flagged, and the sync indicator tells you there is
  something to review. Nothing is discarded and nothing is silently overwritten — but the app
  does not interrupt you to ask which to keep, because by then you are somewhere else.
- Everything works offline, including dates and search, because the app keeps a full local copy.

## Reminders

**Mine cannot notify you while it is closed.** No browser can schedule a notification for later;
this is a platform limitation, not a missing feature. Alerts are stored with each entry and
exported, and they fire while the app is open. The summary on the tile screen is the reminder.

## Updates

When a new version is deployed the app shows "Update ready — reload". It never updates while you
are in the middle of editing.

**Do not use the tarball.** `GET /tarball/{ref}` 302-redirects to `codeload.github.com`, which
answers `access-control-allow-origin: https://render.githubusercontent.com` — one specific
foreign origin. `fetch()` applies CORS to the final response after the redirect, so it is
blocked, and the preflight an authenticated request needs returns 403. `api.github.com/graphql`
by contrast sends `allow-origin: *` and a 204 preflight allowing `Authorization`.

**A repo with no commits rejects the Git Data API outright.** Not just the ref read — `POST
/git/blobs` itself answers 409 "Git Repository is empty", so there is nothing to build a tree
from. Only `PUT /contents/{path}` can create the first commit. The first queued file goes that
way, and everything after drains normally once a history exists.

## Pull

1. `GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{branch}` with `If-None-Match`. A 304 means nothing changed and
   costs no rate-limit quota, and no ETag at all means a first mirror.
2. On 200: fetch the tree, diff blob SHAs, fetch only changed files, drop deleted paths.

Run on app open and on window focus. Background Sync does not exist in Safari, so all syncing is
foreground.

## Writes — one commit per drain

Queue each change locally with the blob SHA it was based on, then drain the whole queue as one
commit via the Git Data API: `POST /git/blobs` per file, `POST /git/trees` with `base_tree`
(deletion = entry with `sha: null`), `POST /git/commits`, `PATCH /git/refs/heads/{branch}` with
the expected old SHA and **no force**.

One drain is one commit, so a move — delete plus create, because the date is in the path and the
API has no rename — cannot be half-applied, and a 20-item offline backlog is one commit.

A rejected ref update means someone pushed elsewhere: pull, rebuild on the new base, retry. This
succeeds, because nearly every write is a create at a freshly generated path.

**True conflict** = a queued change whose base SHA no longer matches the remote blob. Remote keeps
the canonical path; the local version is committed beside it as `<name>.conflict-<yyyymmdd>.md`
with `conflictOf:`. Nothing is discarded and the queue never jams. On 401/403, pause and send the
user to settings.

## Service worker

Registered `{type: 'module'}` so it can import `shared/apps.js`. A version constant names the
cache; install precaches the shell. Same-origin requests are cache-then-revalidate.

Requests to `api.github.com` **bypass the worker entirely** — caching an API response would hand
back a stale ETag and silently break sync.

A new worker waits; the UI offers "Update ready — reload" and `skipWaiting()` runs only on tap.

**The offer is gated on the version, not on a worker waiting.** The worker answers a `version`
message over a `MessageChannel` port with its `VERSION` constant, and the page compares the
waiting worker's answer with the active one's; equal answers mean no banner. A worker that is
byte-identical to the running one can sit in `waiting` indefinitely, and `reg.waiting` alone as
the condition is what makes the banner appear on an app with no update and never go away. A
worker too old to answer reports `null` after a 1.5 s timeout, which differs from a real version
and so still offers the update.

I read the sync path before asking anything. Here's what the code actually says:

**Why it never clears.** `calendar/app.js:280` — `refresh()` runs on open and on every window focus, and its first line is:

```js
if (await queuedCount()) return showSync();   // → "14 change(s) pending"
```

So a non-empty queue means **no drain is ever attempted again, and no pull either**. `drain()` only ever runs from `S.push(...)`, i.e. at the moment of a write. If that one push failed (offline, 401, 403, flaky network), the 14 items sit there forever and the app also stops pulling. `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md:78` and `REQUIREMENTS.md:95` both promise the opposite ("sent when you are back online or reopen the app").

**Why you can't see why.** The failure reason is written only to the `#sync` text node by `push()`'s catch. The next focus event overwrites it with "14 change(s) pending". Nothing persists the error — not the message, not the status code, not the time. There is no record anywhere of what went wrong.

**A second, nastier one.** `drain()` does `clearQueue()` *after* `PATCH /git/refs`. If it dies between those (network drop, tab closed), the commit landed but the queue kept the items with now-stale `baseOid`s. The next drain sees `live !== it.baseOid` and treats your own just-committed work as a true conflict, writing `.conflict-<date>.md` files. So a stuck queue doesn't just sit there — it can manufacture conflicts when it finally runs.

Now the first fork.

This is what REQUIREMENTS.md:95 and TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md:78 already promise, and it is the single change that would have stopped your 14 from accumulating. Risk: a push you didn't ask for at a moment you didn't choose — but every one of those 14 was already an edit you made and the app already told you it was queued.

content.text:
Noted: `refresh()` will always attempt the drain, on open and on focus, with no special-casing for 401/403.

That makes the ordering inside `refresh()` the next decision, and it isn't cosmetic. A `pull()` while the queue is dirty rewrites the local mirror from the remote: for a queued `put`, `putFile` kept the file at its **base** oid, so if the remote moved, the pull overwrites your unpushed text in the mirror (the queue still holds it, and `drain()` will later commit it as a `.conflict-` file — nothing is lost in the repo, but the edit vanishes from the view until then). For a queued `del`, the pull re-adds the file you deleted.

questions.question: Inside refresh(): when the drain attempt fails, should it still go on to pull?

options.label: Drain first; pull only if it succeeded (Recommended)
options.description: refresh() = drain if pending → pull only on success. Keeps the mirror coherent with the queue, so a queued edit never disappears from the view. Costs almost nothing: every realistic drain failure (401, 403, offline, 5xx) would fail the pull too, since both go through the same token and network. The old 'frozen sync' bug can't come back, because the drain now actually runs.

options.label: Always pull, even after a failed drain
options.description: Incoming changes keep arriving whatever the queue is doing. Strictly more up to date, but introduces the window above: a remote change to a path you have queued wipes your unpushed text from the view until the next drain writes it back as a .conflict file.

options.label: Pull first, then drain
options.description: Rebases the queue on fresh data before committing, so drain's own retry-after-409 path fires less often. But it is the worst case for the overwrite window above, and it delays your pending work behind a network read.

content.text: Next: the spurious-conflict bug. If `drain()` dies after `PATCH /git/refs` but before `clearQueue()`, the work is committed but the queue still holds it with stale `baseOid`s, and the next drain writes your own work out as `.conflict-` files. The conflict branch already fetches the live blob, so the fix can be nearly free.

questions.question: How should drain() tell 'someone else changed this' apart from 'I already committed this and never got to clear the queue'?

options.label: Compare the blob text; identical → drop the item (Recommended)
options.description: In the conflict branch, where the live blob is already being fetched, add: if decode(blob.content) === it.text, the remote already has exactly our bytes — this item is a receipt for a commit that landed, so drop it instead of forking a .conflict file. Two lines, no extra requests, and it is correct in the general case too (an identical edit made on another device is genuinely a no-op). Queued deletes are already safe: the path is gone from the remote tree, so !live skips them.

options.label: Record the commit sha before the ref PATCH and reconcile on next drain
options.description: Persist 'attempting commit <sha> for these items' in kv, then on the next drain check whether the branch contains that sha and clear the queue if so. More faithful bookkeeping, but it is new persistent state plus an extra API read on every recovery, to answer a question the blob comparison already answers.

options.label: Delete queue items one by one as each is applied
options.description: Switch queued() to getAllKeys and delete per item instead of clearQueue(). Narrows the window but does not close it — the commit is one atomic act covering all items, so a death mid-loop still leaves some items behind with stale baseOids.

content.text: Now the part you actually asked for. Today nothing survives a reload, which is why you're staring at a bare count. Two kinds of fact are missing: *what went wrong last time* (never persisted at all) and *when each change was queued* (`write()`/`remove()` in `shared/github.js` enqueue `{op, path, text, baseOid}` with no timestamp — so your existing 14 have no age, and no backfill is possible).

options.label: Last error + stamp new queue items (Recommended)
options.description: On any drain failure write kv 'sync.lastError' = {at, message, status, count}; clear it on success. Separately add at: Date.now() to the items enqueued by write()/remove(), so the panel can say 'queued 6 days ago'. Your current 14 predate the field and will read 'queued before this version' — honest, and the field pays off from the next edit on. Both are small and both are needed: the error says why, the age says since when.

Smallest change and it answers your literal question ('cannot see why'), but the panel can never tell a 20-minute offline backlog from a queue that has been wedged for a fortnight — and that distinction is the difference between 'wait' and 'something is broken'.

content.text:
Careful here — this is where a convenience button can corrupt the mirror. Dropping a queued `put` without repair leaves `files` holding your unpushed text at the **base** oid; the next `pull()` compares that base oid against the unchanged remote sha, finds them equal, and skips the path. The divergent text then lives in the local mirror forever, never pushed and never reconciled. So any discard must also repair: forget the local copy and null `commitEtag` so the next pull re-fetches the remote truth.

Also relevant: one drain is one commit, all-or-nothing, so isolating a single item only helps if exactly one item is the problem — and the common failures (401, 403, offline) poison the whole queue equally.

questions.question: What destructive action, if any, does the panel offer when the queue is genuinely wedged?

options.label: One 'discard all pending' with confirm + mirror repair (Recommended)
options.description: Collect the queued paths, clearQueue(), delFile() each of those paths, null commitEtag, then pull — the mirror comes back to exactly what GitHub holds and the count goes to zero. Needs no new store API and matches drain's all-or-nothing nature. Guarded by a confirm naming the count, since this is the one button in Mine that can lose work you made.

options.label: Per-item discard as well
options.description: A trashcan per queue row, so 13 good changes can go while one bad one is dropped. Needs getAllKeys in store.js and a dequeue(key); same repair per path. More control, more code, and of limited use given a drain is one atomic commit.

options.label: No discard — 'push now' only
options.description: The panel can explain and retry but never destroy. Smallest and safest surface; a permanently poisoned queue would then need 'Remove the repo settings' on the Mine home screen, which nukes the whole database.

All branches resolved. Here's the shared understanding.

## Root cause

Your 14 are stuck because **nothing ever retries**. `drain()` runs only from `S.push()` at the moment of a write; `refresh()` — the one thing that runs on open and focus — early-returns the instant the queue is non-empty, so it neither pushes nor pulls. One failed push (offline, expired token, flaky network) wedges that browser permanently, and the reason was written to a text node that the next focus event overwrote. Both requirements docs already promise otherwise (`REQUIREMENTS.md:95`, `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md:78`).

## Plan

**Cause (so it stops happening)**
1. `calendar/app.js` `refresh()`: if the queue is non-empty → `drain()`, report the outcome, and pull **only if the drain succeeded**. Unconditional, on open and on every focus, including on 401/403.
2. `app.js:69-79` (home screen): the same three lines — shared queue, so it drains from whichever screen you open. No panel there.
3. `shared/github.js` `drain()`, in the conflict branch where the live blob is already fetched: if its text equals the queued text, the remote already has our bytes — drop the item instead of forking a `.conflict-` file. Closes the window where a death between `PATCH /git/refs` and `clearQueue()` makes the app fight its own committed work.

**Record (so you can see why)**
4. `shared/github.js` writes one kv record, `sync.last` = `{at, lastAt, count, app, op, outcome, status, detail}`, around both `drain()` and `pull()`. Same op+outcome+status as the stored record → bump `count` and `lastAt`; anything different replaces it; a 304 no-op pull writes nothing. Reads as "403 Forbidden ×12, first 09:14, last 17:40". No ring buffer.
5. `write()`/`remove()` enqueue `at: Date.now()`.

**Tool (`logs`, third row in the hamburger)**
6. Centred panel, built in `calendar/settings.js` (no new file, so `shared/apps.js` is untouched), markup in `index.html`. Three bands: state line + `push now`; one row per queued item (`put`/`del`, path, age — your existing 14 read `—`); the `sync.last` record.
7. `discard all pending` — native `confirm()` naming the count, then `clearQueue()`, `delFile()` on each queued path, null `commitEtag`, pull. The repair matters: dropping a queued `put` without it leaves divergent text in the mirror at the base oid, which every future pull skips.
8. `#sync` becomes a `<button>` that opens the panel.

**Verification**
9. Seven checks in `test/check.mjs`, including the rewrite of the `['filter','settings']` assertion at line 740 and the discard path with `window.confirm` stubbed over CDP. Plus the 320 px fit check with a backlog. `sw.js` `VERSION` bump.

Two things I'm assuming unless you say otherwise: I'll add a line each to `REQUIREMENTS.md` ("Using it") and `TECHNICAL-REQUIREMENTS.md` (Writes), since both currently describe a retry that doesn't exist; and `shared/github.js` gaining the log means `store.js` is untouched.

One honest limitation: the record starts empty, so it can't tell you retroactively why your 14 wedged. But step 1 means the next time you open that browser it will attempt the drain immediately — and whatever comes back lands in `sync.last` for the panel to show. You'll have the answer within one app open.
